title: WorkspaceV5
description: The root identity record of a Writing Intelligence v5 workspace. It exists so that every node, edge, proof and release bundle produced under a `.wi/` directory can name the workspace it belongs to, the schema generation it was written under, and the core build that wrote it. One row of the `workspace` table in `scripts/wi.py` (`DDL`), created by `wi init` and read by every later command. Without this record a bundle could be verified for internal consistency and still not say which project it describes or which rules generation produced it.

id.description: Logical id of the workspace, derived by `logical_id("workspace", <absolute root path>)`. Content-derived rather than random so that re-initializing the same directory yields the same identity and a rebuilt bundle stays byte-reproducible.

title.description: Human-readable project title. Defaults to the workspace directory name when `wi init --title` is not given. Display only; nothing keys off it.

created_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant at which `wi init` created the workspace. The earliest point any state in this workspace can honestly claim.

schema_version.description: The v5 schema generation these records were written under. Bound into every `state_digest` preimage, so a schema bump changes every state digest by construction rather than by convention.

core_version.description: Version of the deterministic core (`scripts/wi.py`) that created the workspace. Recorded so a reviewer can tell which build produced a given proof, and so a version skew is visible instead of inferred.

mode.description: The workspace default evidence mode, set by `wi init --mode`. A project-level policy file may narrow it further; individual commands may override it per invocation, and the override is recorded in the release manifest rather than in this row.

logical_id.description: A UUID-shaped, content-derived logical identity produced by `logical_id()`. Stable across states of the same thing; never random.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 instant with an explicit UTC offset, as emitted by `_now()`.

evidence_mode.description: The five evidence modes from references/v5/POLICY_AS_CODE.md. `off` runs craft passes only; `light` extracts and lists claims without a verdict; `standard` classifies and flags but the verdict is advisory; `strict` enforces the verdict and requires a resolvable anchor or a stated qualification for every factual claim; `regulated` is strict plus contradictions blocking rather than holding and every proceed-anyway recorded as a waiver. The executable gate in `scripts/wi.py` accepts light, standard, strict and regulated.
